data: This is a one-term course in certain core areas of macroeconomics that could not be covered in some detail in Macroeconomics I and Macroeconomics II. In seeking to first establish a strong foundation in economic analysis, and in macroeconomic analysis in particular, the preceding two courses in macroeconomics stayed away from controversies in macroeconomic theory between different schools of thought. Further, some important parts of applied macroeconomic theory, like financial markets and financial crises, could not be dealt in detail in the earlier courses. This course will seek to give a more detailed treatment to these foregoing topics. A serious student of economics should not shy away from controversies and unsettled issues in macroeconomics, and should have the confidence to apply his knowledge to popular and important topics like financial markets and financial crises. The focus in this course will be on certain specific topics that any serious student of economics must have knowledge of. Six topics have been chosen for inclusion in this course at an intermediate level: different approaches to macroeconomic theory, theories of business cycles, macroeconomic policy, financial markets, macroeconomic crises and economic growth theory. This course will be pitched at a level that acts as a bridge, for the undergraduate student to continue onto graduate level studies, and also for those who wish to pursue other avenues like business management and employment as economic analysts. Students in this course will be required to do group projects that shall be designed to give a hands-on experience in using software tools for macroeconomic analysis with these objectives in view.
